locations.name: The Buried Street
locations.description: An intact 19th-century street below the current grid
locations.notes: Sealed entrance found by construction; city records of its excavation are false

locations.name: St. Peter's Catholic
locations.description: Refuge, gathering point, oldest continuously operating building in the Bottom
locations.notes: The basement has been locked since 1943. Hruska has never asked why.

locations.name: Morrow's Books
locations.description: Used and rare books; local history section unusually complete
locations.notes: Has a copy of a book that was never published

locations.name: The Old Market Site
locations.description: Former slave market; memorial marker; active gentrification pressure
locations.notes: The Overwrite is most visible here — the marker sometimes reads different names

locations.name: Serrano's Entry
locations.description: Access point to the canal tunnels from the Bottom
locations.notes: Location known to Declan Morrow. Cost: a Debt.

locations.name: Hollywood Cemetery
locations.description: Maze-like; overlooks the James; presidents and Confederate generals
locations.notes: New sections Emmett does not remember. One grave has a recent date for a living person.

locations.name: Maison Rouge
locations.description: Mireille's gallery and salon. Converted Victorian mansion. Hosts evening salons where art, politics, and supernatural business intertwine. The basement wine cellar has been... expanded.

locations.name: Threshold
locations.description: Asha's vintage shop on Ellwood. Specializes in "authentic" pieces from different eras. The changing room is a Hedge Door (currently unsafe — opening onto unfamiliar ground for three weeks).

locations.name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
locations.description: Major cultural institution. Vera Solis works in the conservation department. Has wings that sometimes appear on floor plans but don't exist in the building.

locations.name: 1708 Gallery
locations.description: Independent contemporary art space. Marcus sometimes shows his Overwrite documentation here, though the pieces tend to "evolve" after installation.

locations.name: Monument Avenue
locations.description: Former Confederate statues created wounds in reality when they were erected, wounds that widened when they were removed. The Hedge grows thin here.

locations.name: Arthur Ashe Monument
locations.description: Stands in stark contrast to the Confederate legacy. Seems to anchor reality more firmly, but something watches from behind the tennis racket's strings.

locations.name: The Empty Plinths
locations.description: Where removed monuments stood. Reality is thin here. Late at night, shapes that might be statues cast shadows.

locations.name: The Fan Historic District
locations.description: Rows of Victorian houses. Many converted to apartments for VCU students. Some houses have more rooms inside than their exterior should allow.

locations.name: Canterbury
locations.description: Exclusive neighborhood. Old Richmond money. Where Power faction members live when they want to be close to Wild energy.

locations.name: Riverfront Plaza
locations.description: Modern office complex. Several law firms have offices here. The building has sub-basements that connect to the old canal system.

locations.name: Federal Courthouse
locations.description: Night faction has cultivated several court staff as assets. Some cases are decided before they're filed.

locations.name: City Hall Annex
locations.description: Where the real municipal business happens, away from the ceremonial main building.

locations.name: James Center
locations.description: Mixed-use towers. Corporate law, financial services, and discrete meeting spaces. Several Night faction fronts operate from here.

locations.name: Canal Walk (Surface)
locations.description: Tourist boardwalk with restaurants and shops. The public face conceals the true nature of what lies beneath.

locations.name: The Old Canal Locks
locations.description: Partially restored, partially flooded. Access points to deeper tunnel systems. Tourist tours end before the interesting parts.

locations.name: Serrano's Domain
locations.description: Network of tunnels beneath downtown. Originally shipping channels, now a vampire court. Heavily defended since the "breach."

locations.name: The Flood Chambers
locations.description: Deeper sections that can be rapidly flooded to prevent intrusion. Serrano's last line of defense.

locations.name: The Exchange
locations.description: Upscale restaurant and bar. Night faction's neutral ground for business meetings. Mortals welcome but carefully watched.

locations.name: The Club at 101
locations.description: Private club in the penthouse of a financial building. Members-only. The real membership list is very different from the official one.

locations.name: Hibbs Hall
locations.description: Philosophy department headquarters. Dr. Olave's office occupies the entire top floor, which has more space inside than the building's exterior suggests.

locations.name: Cabell Library
locations.description: Massive research library. Special Collections contains books that shouldn't exist. The basement levels extend deeper than official plans show.

locations.name: Harris Hall
locations.description: Mathematics building. Prof. Tanaka's office overlooks Monroe Park. She has whiteboards covered in equations that describe impossible geometries. *Olave's closed faculty meetings are held here.*

locations.name: Fine Arts Building
locations.description: Art history department has a private collection of Richmond artwork that shows different scenes depending on when you look at them.

locations.name: Main Hospital
locations.description: VCU Health's primary facility. Power faction uses medical access for research into life, death, and consciousness.

locations.name: Medical Education Building
locations.description: Where Power faction members train new mages in the intersection of magic and medicine.

locations.name: Research Labs
locations.description: Cutting-edge facilities that sometimes produce impossible results. The ethics review board has learned not to ask too many questions about certain projects.

locations.name: The Observatory
locations.description: Hidden facility built into the structure of multiple university buildings. Accessible through a network of maintenance tunnels and forgotten sub-basements. Contains the true Consilium library and ritual spaces.

locations.name: Monroe Park
locations.description: Central campus green space. The ley line beneath the park has run measurably off-tempo three times in six weeks. Power faction monitors this closely.

locations.name: The Commons
locations.description: Student center and gathering space. The Power faction monitors student population for potential Awakening candidates.

locations.name: Creighton Renaissance (Phase A)
locations.description: New mixed-income units where displaced families have returned. Some units overlook spaces where the old buildings still exist in parallel time.

locations.name: The Courts
locations.description: Remaining original buildings scheduled for demolition. Families live knowing their homes have expiration dates. Some buildings appear empty but show signs of ongoing habitation.

locations.name: Transition Housing
locations.description: Scattered sites where displaced families wait for new units. RRHA vouchers sometimes lead to addresses that don't exist on current maps.

locations.name: East End Family Resource Center
locations.description: Provides services, food pantry, and meeting space. Sister Catherine's domain. Sometimes serves families who died years ago but still need help.

locations.name: Oakland Cemetery
locations.description: Historic African-American cemetery that borders the community. Graves sometimes show fresh flowers on plots that have been empty for decades.

locations.name: Corner Stores
locations.description: Neighborhood markets that serve as informal community hubs. Owners know everyone's business and notice when temporal anomalies affect their customers.

locations.name: The Old Armstrong Site
locations.description: Former high school being developed as mixed-income housing. Construction workers find classrooms with lessons still on the boards.

locations.name: The Playground That Wasn't
locations.description: Children play on equipment that doesn't appear in any development plans, but has been there "forever" according to residents.

locations.name: Nine Mile Road Overpass
locations.description: Where the community connects to the wider city. Graffiti sometimes appears in styles from decades past, depicting events that haven't happened yet.

locations.name: The Historic District
locations.description: 19th-century worker cottages on narrow lots. Some houses show room additions from multiple time periods existing simultaneously.

locations.name: Student Blocks
locations.description: Rental properties near VCU campus. Landlords sometimes collect rent for apartments that existed in previous configurations of the buildings.

locations.name: The Old Families
locations.description: Long-term residents in houses passed down through generations. These families anchor the community's memory and cultural continuity.

locations.name: St. Andrew's Episcopal Church
locations.description: Built with Grace Arents funding in 1894. Services sometimes include parishioners from different eras of the neighborhood's history.

locations.name: William Byrd Community House
locations.description: Provides social services and meeting space. Programs occasionally serve participants who died years ago but continue attending.

locations.name: Arents Free Library
locations.description: Small neighborhood library. Books sometimes include local histories that describe events before they happen.

locations.name: Byrd Park Overlook
locations.description: Scenic views of the James River where residents gather. Sometimes shows industrial landscape from the valley's manufacturing heyday.

locations.name: The Art Collective
locations.description: Informal spaces where local artists work and display. Exhibitions sometimes include work by artists who haven't moved to the neighborhood yet.

locations.name: Home Studios
locations.description: Many residents work from converted garages and basements. Musicians hear echoes of industrial rhythms in their compositions.

locations.name: Hollywood Cemetery Border
locations.description: The neighborhood's western edge where residents walk among Civil War graves and famous burials. New graves occasionally appear for living residents.

locations.name: Tredegar Overlook
locations.description: Views of the old iron works site below. Workers sometimes appear at the historical park, continuing shifts that ended 150 years ago.

locations.name: The Expressway Cut
locations.description: Where the Downtown Expressway carved through the neighborhood in the 1970s. The road sometimes shows different routes or doesn't exist at all.

locations.name: The Nail
locations.description: A bar on Idlewood Avenue where information is charged by the drink.

locations.name: Cutler's Gym
locations.description: A boxing gym on Decatur Street and one of Jacob Boone's mortal anchors.
